runs.content:
## New investigation idea
- **[2026-11-11] Health has not changed since 08-03, and its "Biomarkers Being Tracked" table is still empty. The only new health material in three months, the Sahar Yousef attention episode Fred finished on 10-31, is filed under Podcasts only. It includes a cheap test whose result Fred's phone already records.** [[health/overview]] lists two sources and [[health/my-protocol]] has had "[to be added]" in every table since 05-01. Earlier ideas here asked for lab tests (homocysteine, Omega-3 Index) and supplements (creatine, 07-05), which need a purchase or a clinic visit, and none has happened. [[podcasts/podcast-diary-of-a-ceo-phone-addiction-scientist-dr-sahar-yousef]] reports that switching the phone to grayscale cut use by about 1 hour a day in her Berkeley lab, and puts context-switching at about 47 seconds per screen and about 2 hours a day lost. Daily screen time and pickups are logged automatically by the phone (Screen Time / Digital Wellbeing), so this is the one marker that needs no lab, no purchase and no new habit to measure. Learning already holds the companion practice: [[learning/source-ferriss-deloading]]'s "screen-free Saturdays", a page this file had never cited. **Concrete step:** note this week's daily screen-time average and pickups as the baseline, run grayscale for 14 days, and enter before/after as the first row of my-protocol's biomarker table (target: about −60 min/day, Yousef's figure). File the Yousef page under [[health/overview]]'s Sources at the same time, so Health gets its first source since August.

## New cross-domain connection
- **[2026-11-11] The 11-06 entry proposed borrowing the Terrain Autobattler's savings rule for the Children's Financial Literacy Game. The same economy also has the opposite button: reroll, which costs 2 gold for a fresh random set of offers. That is the variable-reward "slot machine" mechanic the Yousef episode Fred just finished warns about. In an autobattler the choice between saving for interest and paying to reroll is the core decision, so this is the save-or-gamble lesson a kids' money game is trying to teach.** [[games/terrain-autobattler-factions-units-economy]] sets the reroll at 2 gold and interest at +1 per 10 held (max +3). It also publishes shop odds by level (level 1–2: 100% 1-cost; 4-costs first at level 5, 2%), and its AI opponents carry a "reroll threshold". [[podcasts/podcast-diary-of-a-ceo-phone-addiction-scientist-dr-sahar-yousef]] describes variable rewards as working like a slot machine and says infinite feeds work by removing stopping points. The autobattler already has the two defences she names. The odds are posted, and the 35-second planning timer ([[games/project-terrain-autobattler]]) is a hard stopping point on rerolling. A kids' version that copies only the savings half would lose the lesson. A copy that keeps rerolls but drops the timer and the posted odds would teach the habit she warns about. **Design rule for `raw/games/Childrens Financial Literacy Game.md`:** keep the reroll, keep both defences, and show the price of each reroll next to the interest it gives up (2 gold spent at 20 held moves the player to 18 and costs the +1 interest on the next round). The 2,000-fight harness extended to full matches (see 11-06) could then measure the reroll threshold at which `aggressive` stops beating `greedy`. That number would be the game's answer to "when is gambling worth it?"

## New investigation idea
- **[2026-11-10] Of Fred's three AI puts, the NBIS put is the one with no backing from its own source. Burry wrote on 08-06 that he skipped NBIS puts because implied volatility above 100% made them too expensive. Fred bought one anyway on 10-01, and by 10-11 Burry had dropped his single-name NBIS short altogether.** [[finance/investor-letters/source-burry-trading-post-2026-08-06]] says Burry shorted NBIS outright at $211.77 and "considered puts but passed", because IV over 100% made the premiums not "make sense". [[finance/trading-portfolio]] shows the $90 Jun-2027 put bought on 10-01 at $5.38/sh (€479). [[finance/investor-letters/source-burry-trading-post-2026-10-11]] then lists Burry's remaining single-name puts as ORCL, MET, CAT and PLTR, and says NBIS was "folded into SMH/NDX". So the ORCL and PLTR puts still copy a live Burry position, but the NBIS put copies one he has closed, in the form he turned down. Three other gaps make the "consider closing NBIS put" line in the 11-09 briefing hard to act on. (1) The put is marked by hand at 80% vol ("Turso row can't be auto-marked") because the options step can't read its strike or expiry, so the ≈€764 mark is a guess. (2) The only AI & Tech pages on Nebius's own business, [[ai-tech/source-meta-nebius-nvidia-27b-deal-2026-08-12]] ($27bn Meta deal) and [[ai-tech/source-reuters-nebius-finland-datacenter-2026-08-11]] ($10bn Finland DC), are headline-only stubs. (3) No thesis of Fred's own is written down. At $141.45 the put is about 36% out of the money and is worth something only because of its long life and high vol. **Next steps:** (a) add the strike, expiry and type to the NBIS option row in Turso so it is marked by the same model as the other two puts. (b) Re-fetch the two Nebius articles with the built-in browser (WebFetch got a 403) and fill in the stubs. (c) Write one sentence on whether this put is Fred's own thesis or a copy of a closed Burry trade. If it is a copy, the 10-11 fold is the exit signal, and the put is currently above its cost.

## New cross-domain connection
- **[2026-11-10] AI & Tech's regional power model rates the Nordics the safest place in the world to power a data centre and lists the projects there. It leaves out the largest one the wiki knows about, Nebius's $10bn Finland build, and Nebius is the company Fred holds a put against.** [[ai-tech/model-dc-power-regional-balance-2026-06-25]]'s EU-3 Scandinavia section rates the region 🟢 LOW risk (firm hydro, cold climate, Nordic wholesale power down ~20% to ~$40/MWh, the cheapest in Europe). Its project table lists only TikTok Finland (€1B) and Mistral Sweden ($1.4B). [[ai-tech/source-reuters-nebius-finland-datacenter-2026-08-11]] records a $10bn Nebius DC in Finland, about seven times larger than either, and it is not in that table. This matters for [[finance/trading-portfolio]]'s NBIS $90 put. Burry's case ([[finance/investor-letters/source-burry-trading-post-2026-08-06]]) is about financing: "off-balance sheet liabilities… uncommenced leases… purchase commitments". It is not about whether the capacity can be delivered. The wiki's main bear argument against neoclouds, power-driven delays (see the DC power tracker), is weakest in exactly the region where Nebius is putting its largest European commitment. A put on NBIS is therefore a pure bet on financing stress. It gets no help from the build-delay risk that hits US-heavy names such as ORCL and CRWV. Two things follow. Adding Nebius Finland to the EU-3 table would make the model's Nordic demand line honest. And any NBIS thesis should say which of the two risks it is betting on.
